messages.subject: fitting covariates with non-linear effect to spatial lgcp with inlabru
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to fit a model using the function lgcp from inlabru, including a random spatial field fitted as a 2d spde using pc priors, and one covariate (to begin with).  The model works relatively well if the covariate is fitted as a linear effect, however I can't get it to work if I try to fit the covariate as a non-linear effect.

I have tried model = "rw1" and "rw2" but for both of them I get an error

Error in inla.check.location(location[[r]], term = gp$random.spec[[r]]$term,  :
  Locations are too close for f(elevation, model="rw1", ...):  min(diff(sort(x)))/diff(range(x)) = 3.191e-08 < 1e-05
  You can fix this by some kind of binning, see ?inla.group
  If you want/need to bypass this check at your own risk, do
> m = get("inla.models", inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m$latent$rw1$min.diff = NULL
> assign("inla.models", m, inla.get.inlaEnv())

This error persists even when changing the mesh to larger or smaller triangles, and when subsampling the point data to 50% of the points and even 10% of the points, or if I try and fit the model just with the covariate, without the spatial field

I have also tried to model the covariate as a 1d spde with 3, 5, 10, and 50 integration points, with and without the 2d spatial field, but also no luck, I get the error

Error in names(marginals.random) <- names.random :
  'names' attribute [2] must be the same length as the vector [1]
Warning in iinla(model = info[["model"]], lhoods = info[["lhoods"]], options = info[["options"]]) :
  iinla: Problem in inla: Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts,  :
  *** Fail to get good enough initial values. Maybe it is due to something else.
iinla: Problem in inla: 1: lgcp(ecomp, setts, domain = list(coordinates = mesh), samplers = samplers,
       options = list(bru_verbose = TRUE))
2: bru(components, lik, options = options)
3: iinla(model = info[["model"]], lhoods = info[["lhoods"]], options = info[[ [...]
4: try_callstack(...)
5: do.call(INLA::inla, inla.options.merged, envir = environment(model$effects))
6: (function (formula = NULL, family = "gaussian", contrasts = NULL,
       data = NULL, quantiles = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), E = NULL,
       offset = NULL, scale = NULL, weights = NULL, Ntrials = NULL,
       strata = NULL, lp.scale = NULL, link.covariates = NULL, verbose = FALSE,
       lincomb = NULL, selection = NULL, control.compute = list(),
       control.predictor = list(), control.family = list(), control.inla = list( [... truncated]
iinla: Giving up and returning last successfully obtained result for diagnostic purposes.

Code for the model and 1d and 2d spde below

# set up 1d mesh
mesh1D <- inla.mesh.1d(seq(min(elev$elevation)-40, max(elev$elevation)+40, length.out = 10),
                       boundary = "free")
# 1d spde
matern1D <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh1D,
                                prior.range = c(200, 0.01),
                                prior.sigma = c(2, 0.05)
)

#2d spde
matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                              alpha = 3/2,
                              prior.sigma = c(1, 0.05),
                              prior.range = c(500, 0.05)
)

# model components
ecomp <- coordinates ~ elevation(main = elev, model = matern1D) +
  mySmooth(coordinates, model = matern)

# run model
efit <- lgcp(ecomp, setts,
             domain = list(coordinates = mesh),
             samplers = samplers,
             options =
               list(
                 bru_verbose = TRUE
             #     control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb", strategy = "gaussian")
               )
             )

Data to run the model can be found here 

Any idea what could possibly be going wrong?

Many thanks,
Virginia

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] fitting covariates with non-linear effect to spatial lgcp with inlabru
parts:
Hi,

Spatial covariates can have a dense set of values, so best to control the model resolution explicitly for rw1 and rw2 models; use e.g. mapper=bru_mapper(mesh1D)
for that.
But that’s effectively also what happens for the spde model you tried, so there may be something else going on as well.
Can you provide a runnable code file using the data you linked to?

Also, what inla and inlabru versions? Have you tried the inlabru devel version?

Finn

Hi Finn,

Yeah, sorry about that, last minute Friday message, I did not think it through.

I have downloaded the inlabru developement version and the latest INLA version, and now the 1d SPDE seems to work. However, I am finding it quite hard to parametrise the 2 spdes (the 1d and the 2d) as slightly changing the priors in one completely changes the posteriors of both. Do you know where I can find an example of how to use mapper=bru_mapper(mesh1D) with the rw2 model? I have tried to find examples online but unsuccessfully, and would like to try and compare it with the spde implementation. Runnable code with this data below just for reference, this now works with the 1d spde but not with the rw2.

####
library(inlabru)
library(INLA)
data <- readRDS("Data/ex_data.RDS")

elev <- data$elev
mesh <- data$mesh
setts <- data$data
samplers <- data$samplers

# create 1d mesh
mesh1D <- inla.mesh.1d(seq(min(elev$elevation)-40, max(elev$elevation)+40, length.out = 100),

boundary = "free")
# 1d spde
matern1D <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh1D,

prior.range = c(800, 0.01),
                                prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01)
)

# 2d spde

matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                              alpha = 3/2,

prior.range = c(500, 0.01),
                              prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01)
)

# model components

comp <- coordinates ~ elevation(main = elev, model = matern1D) +
  mySmooth(coordinates, model = matern)

# fit model
fit <- lgcp(comp, setts,

domain = list(coordinates = mesh),
            samplers = samplers,
            options =
              list(
                bru_verbose = TRUE
                # control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb", strategy = "gaussian")
              )
)

summary(fit)
####

Many thanks!
